title: Every Part Has Its Role: Part-of-Speech Effects in LLM Post-Training
abstract: arXiv:2610.29843v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are typically trained with next-token prediction (NTP), which rewards predicting specific tokens rather than explicitly accounting for the semantic similarities between different words or expressions. Prior work has addressed this limitation by augmenting training data with minimally varying sentences that replace a target word with conceptually related alternatives, e.g., "The tired coach ran home" $\rightarrow$ {"The tired trainer ran home", "The tired instructor ran home", ...}. Such concept augmentation improves performance, but it remains unclear whether its effectiveness depends on where in the sentence the concept is expressed. We reproduce and extend prior work $\textit{beyond nouns}$ to verbs and adjectives, asking whether the part of speech (POS) carrying the concept signal affects perplexity and downstream performance. translated_title: 每个部分都有其作用：词性对大语言模型后训练的影响
translated_abstract: 大语言模型通常采用下一词元预测（NTP）进行训练，这种方式奖励对特定词元的预测，而非显式地考虑不同词语或表达之间的语义相似性。先前的工作通过在训练数据中增广“最小变化句子”来解决这一局限，即将目标词替换为概念上相关的替代词，例如 "The tired coach ran home" → {"The tired trainer ran home"、"The tired instructor ran home"……}。这种概念增广方法能够提升性能，但其有效性是否取决于概念在句子中的表达位置，目前仍不清楚。我们复现并扩展了先前的工作，将其从名词拓展到动词和形容词，探究承载概念信号的词性（POS）是否会影响困惑度和下游性能。我们发现不同的评估设置呈现出不同的模式：概念增广提升了困惑度……（原文摘要到此截断）
tldr: 该研究将概念增广方法从名词拓展到动词和形容词，发现承载概念的词性会影响大语言模型后训练中的困惑度和下游性能，表明不同词性在训练中扮演着不同角色。
en_tdlr: Extending concept augmentation beyond nouns to verbs and adjectives, this study reveals that the part of speech carrying the concept signal affects perplexity and downstream performance in LLM post-training.
